providers.follow_up: Seven of these eight are real dated funds that will open. They are worth staging as a second batch once Paul has seen the first two, rather than adding eight hidden rows to the review queue during launch week.
providers.deliberate_exception_shared_apply_url: Both Kirklees rows carry the same apply_url because One Community publishes no per-fund pages. This is NOT the front-door defect and must not be 'fixed' by merging them. The defect is ONE row standing in front of SEVERAL funds, which hides the funds behind it. Two rows behind one URL hide nothing. Merging them would force one row to average two deadlines (2 October and 6 November), two amounts (£2,000-£10,000 and up to £3,000) and two purposes (council-funded community coordination, and a general community grants pool), which is exactly the averaging that made the Firstport and Leeds front-door rows wrong. Same reasoning as Paul's 8 September one-row-per-programme ruling. Confirmed independently by grant-tracker-be.

two_ridings_followup.correction: An earlier claim of mine in this job was wrong and is withdrawn. I reported Two Ridings as unreadable to both fetch and browser. It bot-walls scripted fetches only; Chrome loads it normally and get_page_text returns full content. 'Bot-walled' has to say walled to WHAT, because fetch-walled and browser-walled are different states and I collapsed them. The nine Two Ridings rows are checkable.

funds_read_in_chrome_2026_09_08.note: LIVE and matching the page on every field checked: £200 to £2,500, income under £150,000, open all year round, covering East Yorkshire, Hull, North Yorkshire and York. This is the row that reaches all four Yorkshire waitlist signups. No change made.

One live row carried deadline 2026-10-12 and amount_max £13,500. Both true of the fund, but of DIFFERENT tiers. The £13,500 Connect and Grow tier gates on an expression of interest at noon on Monday 14 September 2026; 12 October is only the deadline for those already shortlisted. The EOI date was present and correct in the row's brief prose, so this was not a factual error in the row, it was a structural one: a date held in prose drives no alert, calendar marker or urgency colour. Split into two live rows.

hull_sheffield_east_riding.asked: Paul, 8 September: can you fill the Hull, Sheffield and East Riding gaps?
hull_sheffield_east_riding.correction_first: My own earlier claim that these three areas had no live coverage was an artefact of my query, not a fact about the catalogue. I filtered location_tag with an exact-match IN list ('Hull','Sheffield','York'...), which missed every row tagged 'Hull and East Yorkshire', 'North Yorkshire and East Yorkshire', 'South Yorkshire' and 'Bridlington'. Re-scored against all 582 live rows, the picture is different.

actual_position.evidence: Sir James Reckitt Charity General Grants scores 72 for Men in Sheds Hull and is tagged 'Hull and East Yorkshire'. Two Ridings Small Grants (£200-£2,500, open all year, income under £150,000) also covers Hull.

Bridlington Cricket has 2 local rows at Good, best Community First Prime Opportunities Fund at 71, plus Fraisthorpe Wind Farm tagged directly to Bridlington and strong national sport funders (Central Social and Recreational Trust 87, Football Foundation 77).

actual_position.verdict: was a real gap, and it was a front door, not a discovery problem
actual_position.evidence: The only local row at Good was SYCF's own front-door row on /apply/search-our-grants, with no amounts and a null description. Behind it the index lists FOURTEEN funds, none of them held.
